subject: Retention parachute & surge cushion proposal — Olive Labs renewal
messages:
From: Sara Nunez <sara@olivelabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@olivelabs.com>
Date: 2028-04-20T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — capacity needs + pricing ask

Hi Ben,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for Aug 1 is coming up and usage has materially increased after the Q1 product launch. We’re expecting a 2.5x spike in inference hours for the next two quarters and need to lock predictable economics before committing to a longer term.

Key asks:
- A short-term rate hold for the next 3 months while we onboard new models
- A surge cushion (either credits or capped overage rates) to smooth unexpected spikes
- Clear path for committed capacity increase without lengthy reprocurement

Can we get a sketch of what Redwood can offer? Happy to schedule 30m next week.

Thanks,
Sara Nunez
Head of Platform Ops
Olive Labs

Attachment: olive_usage_snapshot_Mar2028.csv (CSV)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nunez <sara@olivelabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-21T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity needs + pricing ask

Sara — thanks for the note and congrats on the strong Q1 launch. We can absolutely put together a retention-focused option that avoids you getting dinged for short-term growth while also protecting our capacity economics.

High-level proposal (sketch):
- 3-month "parachute" rate hold: existing rates preserved for 90 days from renewal effective date
- Surge cushion: 250k token-credit (or equivalent $ value) to absorb spikes, followed by a capped overage of 15% discount to our normal overage rate for the remainder of the first quarter
- Committed uplift path: ability to add committed GPU hours with 30-day notice; price ladder defined in a term sheet

If that sounds directionally right, I’ll loop in Monica to formalize a term sheet and share a workbook with cost scenarios. Can you do Wed 4/24 10:00am PT for a quick alignment?

—Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: (none)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal conversation — capacity needs + pricing ask (Olive Labs)

Monica / Marissa — forwarding Olive Labs' ask. High-level they want a short-term rate protection + surge credits and an easy path to expand commits.

My suggested commercial approach (please advise):
- 90-day parachute rate hold (preserve current per-token rate) tied to a conditional renewal signature today (term to start Aug 1)
- Surge cushion = 250k token-credits or $40k credit (which is more practical?)
- Overages during the 90-day window billed at existing rate but capped with a 15% discount post-credit exhaustion
- Option to add dedicated capacity with 30 days’ notice; discounts laddered by committed tier

Questions for Pricing/Ops:
1) Is a 250k token-credit conservative/too large given their usage file?
2) Can we formalize the 30-day uplift path without rearchitecting their deployment?
3) Any SLA exceptions we should avoid?

I’ve penciled a Wed 4/24 call with Sara. Monica, can you draft a term sheet and a cost workbook for the call?

—Ben

On 2028-04-21 09:24, Ben Carter wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the note...

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-23T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal conversation — capacity needs + pricing ask (Olive Labs)

Thanks Ben — drafted an initial term sheet and a conservative credit proposal. See highlights below and the attached workbook for the scenario math.

Monica's recommended structure (for 4/24 call):
- Parachute rate hold: 90 days at current MSRP (no retroactive credits), must sign the renewal amendment by May 15 to qualify
- Surge cushion: $35,000 one-time credit applied to overage charges; after credit is used, overages billed at existing overage rate less 15% for the remaining 90-day window
- Committed uplift: add-on commitment with 30-day activation; guaranteed capacity assignment on dedicated pool if uplift >= 50% of prior committed baseline
- Performance guardrail: we keep standard SLOs; any bespoke SLA escalations routed to Marissa for executive approval (we should avoid hard SLA credits for this parachute)
- Procurement ask: Olive signs a short addendum (MOP) and issues PO within 10 business days once they accept the term sheet

Attachments included: parachute_term_sheet_v1.xlsx (contains cost scenarios and sample language)

Notes/questions:
- Karthik: is $35k credit within acceptable range for a mid-market retention concession?
- Marissa: if they request SLA credits for outages during the parachute, we should push them to the standard SLA route — avoid comping downtime as part of this concession.

If that looks OK I’ll convert the workbook into a one-page term sheet and send to Sara post-call.

—Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachment: parachute_term_sheet_v1.xlsx (XLSX)

On 2028-04-22 11:05, Ben Carter wrote:

From: Sara Nunez <sara@olivelabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@olivelabs.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-26T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity needs + pricing ask

Ben / Monica — thanks for the clear proposal and for walking us through the options on the call today. Olive Labs is aligned with the parachute structure with two conditional asks:

1) The $35k surge cushion is acceptable; we'd prefer it as token-credit applied first to burst traffic.
2) We need written confirmation that the 30-day uplift path does not require a re-provisioning fee or migration project cost if we stay on Redwood-managed runtime.

If you can send a 1-page addendum with the parachute language and the MOP (procurement template), we’ll sign and push the PO. We’d like the renewal amendment executed by May 12 to meet our internal budget cycle.

Next steps agreed:
- Monica to send 1-page addendum + MOP template (due EOD 4/27)
- Olive to review and sign; issue PO within 5 business days of receipt
- Ben to update HubSpot deal and attach signed docs

We appreciate the flexibility — this will let us expand aggressively in Q3 without surprise infra cost.

Best,
Sara
Head of Platform Ops, Olive Labs

Attachment: signed-mop-template.pdf (PDF)
